F.M.A. No. 531 of 1991.
(With Civil Rule No. 197(fm) of 1991)
lawyer: Mr. Md. Marfat Ali, Advocate, with Mr. Giasuddin Ahmed, Advocate ------ For the Appellants. No one ------ For the Respondent.
parties:
Md. Mamrul and others ------ Appellants.
Vs.
Budhan Mohammad ------ Respondent.
full_judgment:
Muhammad Ansar Ali, J.: This First Miscellaneous Appeal is directed again the judgment and order dated 17.7.1991 passed by the learned District Judge, Thakurgaon, in Miscellaneous Case No. 38 of 1985, under Order, 39 Rule 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure finding the present defendants appellants guilty of disobedience of an order of ad-interim temporary injunction dated 18.11.80 of the lower appellate Court and detaining them in Civil Prison for one month each. The facts leading to the Miscellaneous Appeal, in short, are as follows:- 

 2. The plaintiff respondents instituted Title Suit No. 238 of 1980 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dinajpur, against the defendant appellants and some others for declaration of title to the suit land as described in the schedule of the plaint. Their case is that they, i.e the defts, have been owning and possessing the suit land on payment of rents there of and their names have also been published in the S.A. Khatians in respect of the said properties, but the defendants threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession from the suit-land claiming title therein, hence the suit. 

 3. During the pendency of the suit, the plaintiffs filed an application under Order 39, rule 1 C.P.C., supported by an affidavit in the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, Dinajpur praying for an order of temporary injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with their peaceful possession in the suit-land. The learned Subordinate Judge, after hearing the application, initially issued a notice upon the defendants asking them to show cause as to why the temporary injunction should not be granted. Twice notice of the said show cause was served upon the defendant-opposite parties, but they did not appear to contest the application for temporary injunction. The plaintiffs petitioners, however, prayed for disposal of the matter of temporary injunction, but the learned Subordinate Judge, after hearing the application, rejected the prayer for temporary injunction by his order dated 22.7.80. Being aggrieved by the said order, the plaintiffs preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 73 of 1980 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Dinajpur. During the pendency of the said appeal, the plaintiffs-appellants-petitioners filed an application on 2.1.82 praying for an ad-interim order of injunction against Respondents 1-18 till disposal of the Miscellaneous Appeal and the said application was numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. 38 of 1985. The learned District Judge, on hearing the application for ad-interim injunction, again issued show cause notice upon the defendants-respondents-opposite parties and at the same time granted an ad-interim order of injunction on 18.11.80 restraining the Defendants-Respondents-Opposite Parties from entering into the suit-land and disturbing the possession of the plaintiffs-appellants therein till hearing of the Miscellaneous Appeal and, thereafter, on hearing both the sides, made the ad-interim order of temporary injunction absolute on 3.12.80. Now it appears from the allegations made in the application of the plaintiffs-petitioners under Order 39 Rule 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure that on 19.12.81, Saturday, corresponding to the 3rd Poush 1388 B.S., the defendants-opposite parties 1 to 14 being armed with weapons, lathis etc. trespassed in the suit-land as described in the schedule and inspite of objection, they cut away and removed Anion paddy of the plaintiffs with the help of buffalo carts from the suit-land in violation of the Court's order of temporary injunction and that the quantity of Amon paddy taken away would not be less than 85 maunds, valued at Tk. 11,000/00, along with the straws valued at Tk. 1,000/00. It was alleged that the defendants opposite parties intentionally violated the order of injunction and caused heavy loss to the plaintiffs-petitioners; that the plaintiff petitioner No. 1, tadbirkar of the case, came to Dinajpur on 20. 12.81 and discussed the matter with his learned Advocate who advised him to file a petition against the defendants opposite parties for violation of the order of injunction and, accordingly, after taking preparation, filed this miscellanenos case on behalf of the plaintiffs2 appellants-petitioners on 2.1.82 in the Court of the learned District Judge, Dinajpur. The Misc. Appeal along with miscellaneous case was thereafter transferred to the newly created Court of the learned District Judge at Thakurgaon for disposal. The Defendants- Respondents Opposite Parties appeared in the appeal as well as in the miscellaneous case to contest both of them. The plaintiffs-appellants-petitioners examined as many as 4 P.Ws. to substantiate and prove the allegations made in the application for violation of injunction and on behalf of the Defendants-Respondents-Opposite Parties, a solitary witness Md. Mamnur Rashid being Opposite Party No. 1 in the Misc. Case was examined as O.P. W. 1. The defence case as transpired from the cross-examination of the P.Ws. and the evidence of O.P.W.1 is that the Defendants Opposite Parties did not enter into the suit-lands for cutting or removing the paddy there from as alleged and they also claimed right, title and possession in the suit land and as such there was no question of violation of any temporary injunction by the Defendant-Respondents-Opposite Parties, that they are innocent and have been falsely implicated in the miscellaneous case for violation of temporary injunction out of enmity and grudge. The learned District Judge, after hearing both the sides and considering the facts and circumstances of the case together with the evidence on record, was pleased to hold that the Plaintiffs-Petitioners were able to satisfactorily prove the case of violation of the temporary injunction as against the 12 Defendants Opposite Parties, but failed to prove the same as against 2 other Opposite Parties, namely, Hafizuddin and, Ismail Mahmud and accordingly, found only those 12 Defendants-Opposite Parties, who are Appellants here, guilty under Order 39 rule 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure for violation of injunction and sentenced them thereunder to suffer one month civil imprisonment each and acquitted the rest 2 as stated above by the impugned judgment and order dated 17.7.91. The defendants-appellants who were opposite parties in the Miscellaneous Case being aggrieved, have preferred the present Misc. Appeal against the aforesaid judgment and order of the learned District Judge, Thakurgaon. 

 4. Mr. Md. Marfat Ali, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendants-appellants, has firstly taken me through the petition of complaint alleging violation of temporary injunction, the evidence on record of both the sides and the impugned judgment and order and then seriously contended that the learned District Judge has committed error of law in not framing proper charges (issues) in this case and as a result there has been miscarriage of justice, and hence, the impugned Judgment and order cannot be sustained in law and the same should be set aside. His next contention is that the learned District Judge has failed to properly consider and appreciate the evidence on record and the facts of the case and wrongly held on mere surmises and conjectures that the Plaintiffs-Petitioners were able to prove their case of violation of injunction against the Defendants-Opposite Parties and as such the impugned judgment and order of punishment are bad and illegal and the same should be set aside. 

 6. Now, with regard to the first point of argument of the learned Advocate for the plaintiffs-appellants to the effect that it is true that the present proceeding for violation of injunction under Order 39, rule 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure has arisen out of a Civil Suit/Appeal, but the said proceeding for violation of injunction is of Criminal nature. Hence, in such a case or proceeding, proper charges (issues) should be framed disclosing all material particulars of the allegations so that the persons allegedly at fault may understand the allegations and take proper defence to meet the charges or allegations. It is the contention of the learned Advocate for the Appellants that in the present case such proper charges (issues) have not been framed by the Court and those which have been framed as issues are quite vague and indefinite and as such the present Defendants-Appellants have been seriously prejudiced thereby and they could not take proper defence. In support of his contention. Mr. Marfat Ali has cited two decisions, one in the case of Momtaz Meah Vs. Mosammat Amirunnessa, reported in 9 D.L.R. 444. In this decision which was in connection with a Civil Rule, it has been observed by a single Judge as follows:- 

 The above decision mainly relates to due service of notice of the injunction order. But in the present case, from the defence, it appears that due service of the notice of the order of injunction is not the point for consideration. Rather it appears from the record that the ad-interim order of injunction in the instant case was ultimately made absolute after hearing both the parties and then the same was also served upon the defendant-opposite parties. But from the trend of cross-examination of the P.Ws. and the evidence of O.P.W.1, the case of the defendants opposite parties as transpired is that they, after passing of the order of injunction, did never enter into the disputed land and /or cut away or remove any paddy from the suit-land as alleged. So, the facts and circumstances of this case are different from those of the case as cited above. However, the principle laid down in the above case is not disputed, but the same does not appear to be of any real assistance to the present defendants-appellants. Mr. Marfat Ali, the learned Advocate, with regard to the necessity of framing proper charges (issued) in the case of trial of violation any person for violation of an order of injunction, has referred to another decision reported in 39 D.L.R. page 260 in the case of Sultan Ahmed Vs. Habibur Rahman Munshi which has been based on another decision in the case of Hatim Vs. Shah Din, P.L.D. 1952(Lah) 77 wherein his Lordship A.R. Cornelins, C.J., as his Lordship was then, observed as follows:- 

 "It is true that the present case lies in the Civil Jurisdiction, but penalties involved are clearly of a criminal nature, and, notwithstanding that no precise procedure has been laid down, it is expected that any Court, which feels called upon to impose these penalties, should proceed as nearly as possible in the same manner as a Criminal Court would proceed; in other words, that at the earliest opportunity, when it has formed the opinion that facts exist which may require the imposition of the penalties, the Court shall put the person at fault on his guard by framing a question or an issue which should embody all the elements of a charge under the Criminal Jurisdiction." 

 Following the above principle, the case reported in 39 D.L.R. was decided and it was noticed that the learned Munsif formulated the following points for determination: 

 1. Is the Misc. Case maintainable in the present form? 

 7. But in the facts and circumstances of the case and the allegations made, the same were found not to be proper and in accordance with law. In the above case in 39 D.L.R., His Lordship of the High Court Division was pleased to hold that: 

 "This type of framing of issue in a vague and general way in deciding a case in a proceeding under sub-rule 3 of Rule 2 of Order 39 of the Civil Procedure Code for the purpose of finding the guilt of the alleged offenders cannot be said to be permissible in law. In a proceeding initiated upon an application under sub-rule 3 of Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure bringing allegation for violation of an injunction order passed by a court against the offenders, the trial Court must frame the issue in such a manner so that all the elements of a charge under criminal jurisdiction find place in the issue so that the persons against whom the allegation of violation of Court's order is brought is in no way misled by such issue and is prejudiced in their trial. 

 8. Now, let me see, how far these decisions help the learned Advocate for the defendants-appellants in this case. It appears from the impugned judgment that the learned District Judge framed the following points for determination (issues) in the Miscellaneous Case: 

 From a reading of the above points for determination, it appears to me in this case that all necessary particulars of the allegations have been brought specifically in the issues, though the same have not been numbered serially. The points for determination (issues) as appearing in the impugned judgment are quite distinct and cannot be termed as vague or indefinite and hence there is no question or chance of the appellant's being prejudiced for such framing of issues. I, therefore, find no substance in the first contention of the learned Advocate for the appellants. 

 9. Now, let me consider the 2nd point canvassed before me by Mr. Marfat Ali, the learned Advocate for the appellants, to the effect that the learned District Judge, without proper consideration and correct appreciation of the materials on the record and the facts of the case, merely on conjunctures and surmises, has found the appellants guilty for violation of injunction or, in other words for willful disobedience to the order of injunction. For examining and appreciating the above submission of the learned Advocate, it is necessary now to go into the evidence on record. As has already been stated that the plaintiffs-appellants-petitioners examined four witnesses in all to prove their allegations. Of these, P.W.1 is Budu Mohammad who was one of the plaintiffs-appellants-petitioners in the Miscellaneous Case. In his deposition, he has named all these 12 appellants except Abu Shama to have been on the disputed land cutting and removing 85 maunds of aman paddy there from. He alleged that the defendants opposite parties came to the suit-lands being armed with dao, lathi, etc. and they did not listen to the objection given by him. He has further stated that the service return of the notices of injunction was in the original record of the case in the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge. In cross-examination, he stated that the paddy cutting was staged at about 7/8 a.m. and he was at his house at that time and he had seen the opposite parties going from the house of opposite party Momrul at 7 a.m. and thereafter he himself followed them for 10/15 minutes along with his brother Sadu Mohammad and there was none on the way and the opposite parties started paddy cutting first in the plot No. 341. 

 He thereafter left the place for his house leaving his brother Sadu Mohammad there. Then he called upon some persons including Majir Uddin P.W.2, Islam P.W.3, Kashem P.W.4 and some others of the village and in collecting 8/10 persons from their houses, it took about one hour time. He stated that the opposite parties were armed with lathi, ballams etc, but the persons whom he, called had no lathi or ballam with them. He stated that when he along with others, went to the place of occurrence, half of the paddy from half of plot No. 341 was already cut away and removed with the help of a buffalo cart. He then specifically stated that Shariful, Mamrul, Siddique, Piar Ali, Ahad Ali, Ismail, Nurul Hoq, Mofizuddin and Idris Ali were cutting paddy. He stated that just after cutting of the paddy, the same was being removed by buffalo cart. He, however, could not say how much time was taken to cut the paddy from the said land. After finishing the cutting of paddy from Plot No. 341, the opposite parties started cutting paddy from plot No. 310 and at that time Mazir P.W.2, Islam P.W.3, Kashem P.W.4 and he himself stood standing on plot No. 341. He further stated that the persons as named above, after cutting paddy from Plot No. 310, started cutting paddy from plot No. 336 and at that time Mazir P.W.2, Islam P.W.3 and Kashem P.W.4 were towards the north of Plot No. 336. He could not say how much time was taken to cut the paddy from that plot and by how many carts the said paddy was removed. He then stated that the opposite parties then cut away paddy from plot No. 654 in another Mouja and at that time his brother and son Babon were there and this way, it was 4 p.m. in the afternoon he saw cutting the paddy from the disputed lands. Then he stated that cutting of paddy in 2 places in Plots Nos. 732 and 736 thus ended before half an hour of the sunset. He stated that Mazir Uddin P.W.2, Islam P.W.3 and their houses were adjacent to his house. He stated that Islam P.W.2 was his nephew by village courtesy. He denied the suggestion that the opposite parties had no lathi or arms with them and he (P.W.1) did not go to the place of occurrence with Nazir P.W.2, Islam P.W.3 and Kashem P.W.4 or any other person as claimed. He also denied a suggestion that the opposite parties did not cut away any paddy from the suit-land and that he started this false case of violation of injunction against the opposite parties Out of sheer grudge and enmity. 

 12. The opposite parties, however, examined only one witness, namely, Aminur Rashid as O.P.W. He stated that on receipt of the information about the order of injunction from the Court some of the opposite parties went to the disputed land for cutting paddy. He denied a suggestion that the opposite parties threatened the plaintiffs with dispossession. He categorically stated that they did not go to the disputed land and cut away any paddy. He also denied a suggestion that they did not obey the Court's order and that they were desperate in nature. He asserted that the plaintiffs started this case falsely only to harass them. He further stated in cross-examination that after passing of the order of temporary injunction dated 18.1.80 they did never go to the disputed land. He strongly denied a suggestion that they cut away paddy on the 3rd of Pous, 1388 B.S, from the disputed land. He also denied a suggestion that he was giving false evidence. 

 13. Now, from a reading of the impugned judgment, it appears that the learned District Judge, without proper discussion of the evidence on record, abruptly came to a finding to the following effect, “প্রার্থী পক্ষের ৪ জন স্বাক্ষীর জবানবন্দী ও জেরা পরীক্ষা করিয়া দেখা যায় যে, প্রতিপক্ষের একজন স্বাক্ষীর জবানবন্দীর চেয়ে প্রার্থী পক্ষের ৪জন স্বাক্ষীর জবানবন্দী বেশী নির্ভরযোগ্য এবং প্রার্থীপক্ষ সন্দেহাতীতভাবে প্রমাণ করিয়াছে যে, জেলা জজ দ্বারা স্বাক্ষরিত অন্তবর্তীকালীন নিষেধাজ্ঞার আদেশ ভংগ করিয়া প্রতিপক্ষগণ নালিশী জমিতে প্রবেশ করে এবং ধান কাটিয়া নিয়া যায়, কাজেই ১২জন প্রতিপক্ষ দেওয়ানী কাঃবিঃ ৩৯ অর্ডার, রুল ২(৩)এর বিধি মোতাবেক শাস্তি পাওয়ার যোগ্য।” From the above, it appears that the learned Judge was swayed more by the number of the witnesses for the petitioners than by their quality or credibility. It is to be remembered that a proceeding under Order 39 rule 2(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure is, in fact, if not fully criminal, then certainly it is quasty criminal in nature and in determining the guilt or otherwise of the persons at fault, the well settled principles for the administration of justice must be followed as enunciated in the decision cited above and in a proceeding like the present one, the person or persons charged must be presumed to be innocent unless his guilt or fault is proved beyond all reasonable doubt and, further, the onus of proving the allegations of disobedience is always on the prosecution. Now, keeping in view the above principles, if the present case is considered vis-a-vis the evidence on record, then it will be found that there are some material discrepancies and contradictions in the evidence of the P.Ws. in respect of the place, time and the manner of occurrence as alleged, giving rise to reasonable doubt as to the case of the petitioners. P.W.1 Badu Mohammad is one of the petitioners who have in his evidence narrated all the allegations against the present appellants opposite parties. He has named firstly 11 persons who allegedly took part in the occurrence. He did not name appellant Abu Shama, though he claims to be an eye witness. About the time of occurrence he stated that the opposite parties were armed with lathi, ballam etc. and they started cutting paddy in Plot No. 341 at 7 a.m. and he had seen them going to the place of occurrence from the house of Mamrul and thereafter and within 10/15 minutes he also went behind the opposite parties with his brother Sadu Mohammad. But the said Sadu Mohammad has not been examined. He stated that he attempted to collect persons, namely, Mazir Uddin, Islam, Kashem etc. first and then saw other persons namely Shariful, Mamrul, Siddik, Piar Ali, Ahad Ali, Ismail, Nurul Huq, Mofizuddin and Idris Ali who were also cutting paddy in the land and then he stated that after completion of cutting in Plot No. 341, the opposite parties started cutting paddy in Plot No. 310 and thereafter in Plot No. 336 and then in some other plots. He could not, however, say as to how much time was taken for cutting paddy from all those plots. Of course lastly he stated that the paddy cutting ended within half an hour before the sunset. He stated that removal of paddy by carts was going on as soon it was cut. Now, in the evidence of the others who claim to be eye-witnesses, we find some different versions. P.W.2 Mazir Uddin stated that paddy cutting was started in plot No. 341 by the opposite parties in the morning before rise of the sun and he could not say anything about cutting of paddy from any other plot except Plot No. 341. He was at the place of occurrence for about 1/1.5 hours. He has not said anything about removal of the paddy from the disputed land by the opposite-parties with the help of any buffalo cart. He has not stated that the paddy of plot No. 341 was already cut away as it was said by P.W.1, but he claims to be an eye-witness and according to P.W.1 he was also with him while the opposite parties were cutting paddy in other plots. Now, it appears that he is a man belonging to the group of the plaintiff’s petitioners. P.W.3 Ismail Uddin has, of course, named 12 persons violating the order of injunction in his deposition in chief, but he stated in cross-examination that he had seen the paddy cutting only in plot No. 341 and not in any other plot. He could not say the name of the owners of the lands around plot No. 341. He stated that he was called upon by badu Mohammad at 8/9 A.M. in the morning and he found 20/25 persons apart from the opposite-parties at the place of occurrence including one Abdul Hye, Dr. Shamsuddin, Gulzar and Joynal, but they have not been made any witness in this case. He also appears to be a man belonging to the group of the plaintiffs-petitioners and he has long standing dispute over the land with the group of Mamrul. He further stated that before finishing paddy cutting he came back home with P.W.1 Badu, but P.W.1 did not say so. He also does not say as has been said by P. W. 1 that after completion of paddy cutting from Plot No. 341, the opposite parties were cutting paddy from Plot No. 310 and other plots and that he along with P.W.1 and others remained standing on Plot No. 341 and 336. P.W.4 Md. Wahidur Rahman was not named by any of the other witnesses. He stated that the cutting of paddy took place on the 3rd of Magh and not Poush at about 3 p.m. and in cross-examination he further stated that cutting of paddy was started after 4 p.m. Thus, from a careful scrutiny of the evidence on record, it appears that the discrepancies and contradictions in the evidence of the P.Ws. with regard to date, time, place and the manner of occurrence are very clear and distinct and in view of such state of the evidence on record, it is not at all safe to rely on such evidence of the P.Ws. for finding the opposite parties, -appellants guilty of the offence of violation of injunction. Again it is not understood why some material witnesses as named by the Plaintiffs-Petitioners, namely Swapan, Sadu Mohammad his brother, his son Kashem have not been examined in this case. At the same time some other witnesses, as named by P.W.3, namely Abdul Hye, Dr. Shamsuddin, Gulzar Hossain and Joynal, who were alleged to be present at the place and the time of occurrence and also the cart-driver who was allegedly utilised by the opposite parties to bring the disputed paddy from the suit-land, have not been produced as witnesses. P.W.1 is one of the plaintiffs-petitioners and as such he is naturally interested and P.Ws. 2, 3 appeared to be the persons belonging to the group of the plaintiffs-petitioners. So, they are not so independent and apart from that there are also material contradictions and inconsistencies in their evidence. Their evidence, therefore, does not inspire confidence and should be taken with a grain of salt, but the learned District Judge, without carefully scrutinising the same in its true perspective, has accepted them as reliable in an omnibus way and illegally found that the petitioners have been able to prove the case of violation of the order of injunction as against the opposite parties beyond reasonable doubt, and further, he has failed to give any weight on merit to the evidence of O.P.W. 1 at all and his evidence have been discarded only because he is the solitary witness and has not been corroborated by any other witness. Thus, from a close scrutiny of the evidence on record, I cannot but disagree with the finding of the Court below and hold that the P.Ws. are not reliable and the plaintiffs petitioners have failed to prove their case of violation of injunction as against the appellant-opposite parties vis-a-vis the place, time and the manner of occurrence. I am, therefore, of the opinion that the learned District Judge has committed illegality in passing the impugned judgment and order against the appellants opposite parties which need be interfered with in the interest of justice and the appellants should be given benefit of doubt.
